### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, the alternatives A19, A21 and A24 (each in roughly 31–36 of 100 traces, seldom more than one per trace) ran before A25 and before A20/A22/A23 — A19 preceded A20 in about 29 of 100 traces and followed it in essentially none — and A25 and A29 preceded A20, A22 and A23 (A25 before A20 in about 98 of 100). In the later window all of these orders are reversed: A20 preceded A19 in about 33 of 100 traces, A22 preceded A21 in about 28 of 100, A20 preceded A24 in about 39 of 100, and A20 preceded A25 in about 98 of 100. [REL047, REL052, REL053, REL058, REL061, REL062, REL063, REL068, REL071, REL078, REL079, REL085, REL092]
- The chain between the two blocks kept its shape in both windows: A25 led to A32 or A33 in about 93–96% of its outgoing transitions, A32 and A33 led to each other and to A26, and A26 → A27 → A28 → A29 held with about 97–98% shares before and after. [DIR025, DIR026, DIR027, DIR028, DIR032, DIR033]
- The hand-offs at the edges changed accordingly: A19, A21 and A24 led to A25 in about 93–97% of their outgoing transitions before and to A30 in about 92–97% after; A20, A22 and A23 led to A30 in about 29–37% before and to A25 in about 28–37% after; A40 led to A19/A21/A24 in about 93% of its outgoing transitions before and to A20/A22/A23 in about 83% after; A29 led to A20/A22/A23 in about 99% before and to A19/A21/A24 in about 98% after. [DIR019, DIR020, DIR021, DIR022, DIR023, DIR024, DIR029, DIR040]
- Mean event positions moved as this exchange implies: A19, A21 and A24 shifted from about 0.36–0.37 to about 0.67 of the trace, A20, A22 and A23 from about 0.64–0.65 to about 0.38–0.39, A25 from 0.39 to 0.45 and A29 from 0.58 to 0.64. [POS005, POS006, POS007, POS008, POS009, POS010, POS011, POS012]
- Lag evidence agrees: the ordered pair A22 → A25 within five steps appeared in 1 trace before versus 200 after (A23 → A25 and A40 → A22 likewise 1 versus 200), while A21 immediately followed by A25 fell from about 97 of 100 such pairs to 2 observed pairs. [LAG040, LAG046, LAG051, LAG068]
- A08 became far less frequent — about 64 of 100 traces before versus about 29 after — and the detour A15 → A08 → A16 largely disappeared: A15 led to A08 in about 39% of its outgoing transitions before versus about 7% after (A15 → A16 rose from about 61% to 88%), A08 led to A16 in about 93% versus 31%, and A08's mean position moved later (about 0.26 → 0.41) with more variable placement. In both windows every A08 occurrence still co-occurred with the always-present activities, so A08 became skippable rather than moved to a separate path. [OCC008, REL001, DIR008, DIR015, POS001, LAG004]
- Several rarely used activities became more frequent: A06 from about 7 to 24, A04 from about 7 to 21, A10 from about 9 to 19 and A02 from about 9 to 16 of 100 traces; A21 declined somewhat (about 36 → 29 of 100), and A42 rose slightly in mean occurrences per trace (0.82 → 0.93) while A43 (0.89 → 0.77) and A44 (0.89 → 0.78) declined. [OCC002, OCC004, OCC006, OCC010, OCC021, OCC038, OCC039, OCC040]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that, in the later window, two blocks of activities exchanged their places around an unchanged middle chain. In the earlier window the process ran one of the alternatives A19, A21 or A24 between A40 and A25, and ran A20, A22 and A23 — always together, in no fixed order — between A29 and A30; in the later window A20, A22 and A23 run between A40 and A25, and A19, A21 and A24 run between A29 and A30, leading directly to A30. The middle chain A25 → A32/A33 → A26 → A27 → A28 → A29 is unchanged, and each block keeps its internal character (A19/A21/A24 remain mutually exclusive alternatives; A20/A22/A23 remain together in mixed order). [REL047, REL048, REL058, REL059, REL062, REL068, REL078, REL092, DIR019, DIR024, DIR029, DIR040]

The exchange is shown directly and consistently: about twenty relation items flip every pairwise order between the blocks and between each block and the chain, each difference lying at the top of about 200 random re-splits of the pooled data; the successor changes at A19/A21/A24, A20/A22/A23, A40 and A29 show the same exchange; and the position shifts match. Participation of every activity involved is essentially stable (A20, A22, A23, A25 and A29 occur in all traces in both windows; A19 about 31 → 33 and A24 about 36 → 39 in 100), so the flips are not explained by the activities becoming rarer, and the unchanged middle chain rules out a bypass of part of the process. [REL047, REL062, DIR019, DIR020, DIR024, DIR029, DIR040, POS005, POS006, POS008, POS009, OCC019, OCC020, OCC022, OCC023, OCC024, OCC025, OCC028]

Limitations: each window is a finite sample of 200 traces, and the evidence establishes that the relative orders flipped but not how the exchange was implemented. The main competing explanation — that the flips are a sampling artefact — is made unlikely by the coherent direction of all relation items together with the matching successor and position changes, but it cannot be fully excluded; the slight decline of A21 (about 36 → 29 of 100 traces) may also be a sampling difference. [OCC021, REL047, REL062, DIR019, DIR040]

Other differences: A08 became far less frequent (about 64 → 29 of 100 traces) and its detour between A15 and A16 was mostly replaced by a direct A15 → A16 transition, with A08's remaining occurrences appearing later and in varied surroundings; in addition, the rare activities A02, A04, A06 and A10 now occur in roughly twice as many traces, and A42, A43 and A44 show small frequency shifts. [OCC008, REL001, DIR008, DIR015, POS001, LAG004, OCC002, OCC004, OCC006, OCC010, OCC038, OCC039, OCC040]
